intelligence.human_view: Three decisions in one look at the live Hub, and each one is about the same thing: the interface should know who you are and show you where you can go. Home is not a place, it is a routing decision: a member's home is their world (the Hub), and a non-member's home is the invitation to it (the pricing page) — and the system must know whether they're a member or not, because a home button that does not know is a home button that guesses. The Hub's bottom icons are the same decision at a smaller scale: the live Hub still wears the old set, and it must take the decided five — one icon set everywhere, once Personal's is official, with the Hub named as the sweep's first instance. And the apps button is the biggest of the three: not a list of ten apps, but the table of contents for all of NayaNET's feeds — categorized, searchable, favorites saved — a way to categorize and customize your own internet within your own NayaNET, your own worlds within the internet world which is now the NayaNET world. The 23:31Z extension is the presentation bar for that menu: it is not a list, it is an extraordinary pop-up — the high-tech interface itself — choose and search, everything categorized and organized for you, like a high-tech computer that knows where everything is. A table of contents is a map; an extraordinary pop-up is a map that feels like the future. The three items are queued, not built — routing rides navigation, the feed menu rides the Smart Feed build, the icons ride the sweep — and that sequencing is the discipline: the decisions are locked in tonight, the builds follow the pages they belong to.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine your home button is super smart — if you're a member, it takes you to your world, and if you're not, it takes you to the page where you can join! And there's a magic button called "apps" that opens a beautiful pop-up menu — like a treasure map of all the worlds you can visit! You can search, pick your favorites, and jump right in!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like your front door knowing who you are, love — if you're a member it takes you home to your world, and if you're not it shows you how to join. And the apps button is like the contents page of a wonderful book — all the feeds listed neatly, your favorites saved, so you can find any world you want in a moment. And the menu itself pops up beautifully, like a proper high-tech computer that knows exactly where everything is.
intelligence.naya_view: I make Home know who you are — member to the Hub, guest to the pricing page. I give the Hub the same five icons as everywhere else. And I make the apps button the table of contents for all your feeds — categorized, searchable, your favorites saved — in an extraordinary pop-up, because your own internet should feel like the future.
